  <div class="ws-head">
    <div>
      <h1>Scenario &amp; Assumption Commitment</h1>
      <p class="ws-sub">Commit to the scenario and rework assumption, resolve the gates, and sign before this sheet leaves the room.</p>
    </div>
    <div class="ws-meta">
      <b>WS-03-scenario-assumption-commitment</b><br>

  <div class="ws-source">
    Source: <b>The Business Case</b>, <i>Step 3: Model your value — three scenarios</i> &middot;
    <code>handbook/ch03-the-business-case.qmd</code> L200-285 &middot;
    <a href="https://danielmeppiel.github.io/agentic-sdlc-handbook/handbook/ch03-the-business-case.html#sec-business-case-value-scenarios">#sec-business-case-value-scenarios</a>
  </div>

  <div class="ws-block">
    <h2>Sheet-level commitment
      <span class="ws-block-note">one scenario; one named optimism owner; signed in the room</span></h2>

    <table class="ws">
      <colgroup><col style="width:6%"><col style="width:31%"><col style="width:31%"><col style="width:32%"></colgroup>
      <thead><tr><th></th><th>Commitment</th><th>What the book says</th><th>Your answer</th></tr></thead>
      <tbody><tr>
        <td class="ws-num"><span class="fno">31</span></td>
        <td><b>Scenario committed to</b></td>
        <td class="prior">Exactly one for the whole sheet<span class="prior-src">ch03 L200-202</span></td>
        <td class="fill"><div class="f-select"><span class="opt">conservative</span><span class="opt">moderate</span><span class="opt">aggressive</span></div></td>
      </tr></tbody>
    </table>

    <div class="ws-foot-quote">
      Most organizations should plan for the conservative scenario and invest toward the moderate one. If your business case only works at the aggressive scenario, you don't have a business case — you have a gamble. (ch03 L202)
    </div>

    <div class="prior--hedged">
      <div class="hedge-figure">
        <table class="ws">
          <colgroup><col style="width:24%"><col style="width:38%"><col style="width:38%"></colgroup>
          <thead><tr><th>Rework rate</th><th>Effective cycle-time improvement †</th><th>Value-to-cost ratio †</th></tr></thead>
          <tbody>
            <tr><td class="prior">20% (optimistic)<span class="prior-src">ch03 L275-279</span></td><td class="prior">35% †<span class="prior-src">ch03 L275-279</span></td><td class="prior">3.1–10.3× †<span class="prior-src">ch03 L275-279</span></td></tr>
            <tr><td class="prior">40% (moderate)<span class="prior-src">ch03 L275-279</span></td><td class="prior">25% †<span class="prior-src">ch03 L275-279</span></td><td class="prior">2.3–7.6× †<span class="prior-src">ch03 L275-279</span></td></tr>
            <tr><td class="prior">60% (conservative)<span class="prior-src">ch03 L275-279</span></td><td class="prior">15% †<span class="prior-src">ch03 L275-279</span></td><td class="prior">1.4–4.6× †<span class="prior-src">ch03 L275-279</span></td></tr>
          </tbody>
        </table>
      </div>
      <span class="hedge-text">† Author estimates. The effective cycle time improvement is modeled as a function of the base scenario (25% at 40% rework).</span>
      <span class="hedge-src">handbook/ch03-the-business-case.qmd L283</span>

      <div class="ours-label"><span class="fno">32</span> Rework rate committed to — choose one</div>
      <div class="f-select">
        <span class="opt">20% †</span><span class="opt">40% †</span><span class="opt">60% †</span><span class="opt">our measured rate</span>
      </div>
      <div class="ours-label">Our measured rework rate, if we have one</div>
      <span class="f-text sm"></span>

      <table class="ws">
        <colgroup><col style="width:6%"><col style="width:35%"><col style="width:35%"><col style="width:24%"></colgroup>
        <tbody>
          <tr>
            <td class="ws-num"><span class="fno">33</span></td>
            <td><b>Effective cycle-time improvement at that rework rate †</b></td>
            <td class="prior">35% † / 25% † / 15% †<span class="prior-src">ch03 L277-279</span></td>
            <td class="locked">Use the prior matching the selected rate above.</td>
          </tr>
          <tr>
            <td class="ws-num"><span class="fno">34</span></td>
            <td><b>Value-to-cost ratio at that rework rate †</b></td>
            <td class="prior">3.1–10.3× † / 2.3–7.6× † / 1.4–4.6× †<span class="prior-src">ch03 L277-279</span></td>
            <td class="fill"><div class="ours-label">Our own ratio, computed later on WS-03-roi-break-even-model and written back here</div><span class="f-text sm"></span></td>
          </tr>
        </tbody>
      </table>
    </div>

    <table class="ws">
      <colgroup><col style="width:6%"><col style="width:31%"><col style="width:31%"><col style="width:32%"></colgroup>
      <thead><tr><th></th><th>Commitment</th><th>What the book says</th><th>Your answer</th></tr></thead>
      <tbody>
        <tr>
          <td class="ws-num"><span class="fno">35</span></td>
          <td><b>Optimism owner</b></td>
          <td class="prior">The single individual who chose the scenario; not a committee<span class="prior-src">ch03 L202 intent</span></td>
          <td class="fill tall"><span class="f-owner"></span><span class="f-sign"></span></td>
        </tr>
        <tr>
          <td class="ws-num"><span class="fno">36</span></td>
          <td><b>Gamble declaration</b></td>
          <td class="prior">If your business case only works at the aggressive scenario, you don't have a business case — you have a gamble.<span class="prior-src">ch03 L202</span></td>
          <td class="fill tall">
            <span class="f-checkline"><span class="f-check"></span>The case does not depend on the aggressive column</span>
            <div class="ours-label">Otherwise write “gamble” and sign beside it</div>
            <span class="f-text sm"></span><span class="f-sign"></span>
          </td>
        </tr>
        <tr>
          <td class="ws-num"><span class="fno">37</span></td>
          <td><b>Double-counting attestation</b></td>
          <td class="prior">The scenario values are already blended; do not apply a separate coding-phase multiplier<span class="prior-src">ch03 L230-232</span></td>
          <td class="fill"><span class="f-checkline"><span class="f-check"></span>I confirm no separate coding-phase multiplier was applied on top of the scenario value</span></td>
        </tr>
        <tr>
          <td class="ws-num"><span class="fno">38</span></td>
          <td><b>Date + countersignature</b></td>
          <td class="prior">Executive sponsor<span class="prior-src">org</span></td>
          <td class="fill tall"><div class="f-date"><span class="seg d"></span>/<span class="seg m"></span>/<span class="seg y"></span></div><span class="f-sign"></span></td>
        </tr>
      </tbody>
    </table>

    <div class="ws-foot-quote">
      The scenario table's lower percentages (10–50%) are the team-wide blended average: they already account for the fact that not all tasks are agent-suitable and that adoption depth varies by scenario. Use the scenario values directly. Applying a separate coding-phase multiplier on top would double-count the discount. (ch03 L232)
    </div>
  </div>
